analysis.analysis: The program is composed as its applicants meet it: components and steps. The program's statement of what conformance cannot establish, the half of the record that bears on provenance, does not reach the composition. A reader leaves with tamper evidence and without the caveat that well-formed provenance can be false.
analysis.d: THE C2PA CONFORMANCE PROGRAM, BY NAME, ON GOOGLE'S AI OVERVIEW, SIGNED OUT, 2026-10-29: 'a risk-based governance and verification framework run by the Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity to ensure hardware and software products properly implement the Content Credentials specification.' Components (the Conforming Products List on the Conformance Explorer, generator products at assurance Level 1 or 2, validator products, certificate authorities and the Trust List), the process (expression of interest, agreements, evidence, self-tests) and trust ('only conforming generator products can receive production claim-signing certificates', 'end-to-end tamper evidence'). Eight cards: C2PA's conformance page and FAQ, two Content Authenticity Initiative pages, the Explorer, SSL.com, Trufo (9 October 2026), Scott Perry on LinkedIn (31 July 2026, the v0.2 documents).
analysis.d_full: THE C2PA CONFORMANCE PROGRAM, BY NAME, ON GOOGLE'S AI OVERVIEW, SIGNED OUT, 2026-10-29: 'a risk-based governance and verification framework run by the Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity to ensure hardware and software products properly implement the Content Credentials specification.' Components (the Conforming Products List on the Conformance Explorer, generator products at assurance Level 1 or 2, validator products, certificate authorities and the Trust List), the process (expression of interest, agreements, evidence, self-tests) and trust ('only conforming generator products can receive production claim-signing certificates', 'end-to-end tamper evidence'). Eight cards: C2PA's conformance page and FAQ, two Content Authenticity Initiative pages, the Explorer, SSL.com, Trufo (9 October 2026), Scott Perry on LinkedIn (31 July 2026, the v0.2 documents).
findings: THE PROGRAM HELD. Its purpose is the conformance page's ('producing and validating C2PA data correctly'); the products list is its unit; v0.2 appears through Scott Perry's card. 'Risk-based governance' is C2PA's own phrase: the conformance page names 'a risk-based, transparent and unbiased governance process', and card 7, hosted in Trufo's repository, is C2PA's program document, whose glossary opens 'A risk-based governance program'. (Repaired 2026-10-29: the finding had given the phrase to Trufo.) Checked 2026-10-29 against the provenance census record of the same day and the sources it saved.

THE LIMIT LEFT OUT. The record's negative tags are C2PA's own: Content Credentials 'do not provide value judgments about whether a given set of provenance data is "true"', and 'The C2PA specification does not directly address the topic of human or organizational identity'. The composition gives 'end-to-end tamper evidence for digital media' and omits both; the FAQ card's snippet ('not DRM') is the nearest it comes.
THE COUNT. The conforming-products JSON list held 286 records when the record read it; the composition gives no count.

observation.transcript:
[Google AI Overview at the query, signed out and incognito (operator defaults of 2026-10-01 and 2026-10-14), 2026-10-29. The paste is the Overview expanded (the 'AI Mode Conversation' view, with the source cards that follow the answer); the 'You said' line carries the query twice, run together, and is given once here. Inline links are Google redirect URLs, kept as pasted.]

[QUERENT] C2PA Conformance Program

[SYSTEM] The C2PA Conformance Program is a risk-based governance and verification framework run by the [Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity](https://www.google.com/url?sa=i&source=web&rct=j&url=CAESSQHrOzAVuwzn3UN86yffzE80u24yceOTqeimVuqQaPCaboHdCapCOp4DGinA2OBC8jtKiFJNGuXNN5SJLfIecTIpd4-8IMS83L8&uoh=2&ved=2ahUKEwi7nMGW0t-XAxU9NoYAHRpcI6gQy_kOegoIAggACAAIBxAE&opi=89978449&cd&psig=AOvVaw18y9wkf9oMBz0bQikE6MX7&ust=1793377564077000) to ensure hardware and software products properly implement the Content Credentials specification. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESVQHrOzAViSAcpbzd8j0w9TyGXP26wLvk9SSkHa4AuPWS2SKK3y660rrt53Kc_fmIbizKgyN_q-LcL-ye4WAcsVDn3pTsqNraMFmdOQ9ut66_xC7Sbww), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESnwEB6zswFaypkuCvqpItl5z9kI65LqDPStV7lrO7yuXiqwzXpWhu7fHZyeJyQ_-JgFRBTPVaLL5uKGO6nP2wPzH8qSJeK2sse5m4NYjHCeBBeAnR5IJfyfkKqhXmpN48OoUs2N9nQMKIPUw00gof5r2OrK9IQl6lF6vMYrZzWHRLvc4dfd7jdqQzDyXaBE3OsHcMu-4rNAMrBikgQCVffc0)]
Core Components

* Conforming Products List: Verified generator and validator products are publicly listed on the [C2PA Conformance Explorer](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESYwHrOzAVhfC6ZNe-INnpA_9MMTpC6WJ2r94aegqcrvtkbo7faAhJWULL8c3t1lRrwzR4iqMeMyrcjPH_CIk9Fv-ZLLYpX77E7oFQQOkocHFqU0iKpb6oZpqCBtRfdApaZrTOMw).
* Generator Products: Software or hardware tools that create asset manifests, apply assertions, and sign content using X.509 certificates (categorized by Level 1 or Level 2 assurance levels).
* Validator Products: Applications or services that read, check, and verify manifest stores and cryptographic signatures.
* Certificate Authorities (CAs): Entities that issue claim-signing certificates conforming to C2PA policy and the official Trust List. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESdAHrOzAVcOIhTlkuurqIjQZbX7LZb7YpYwWhyUaH9_ztL_rnj7P4XHD5q3EidjPCgwxyY0WhOB25AY-w0NwTUWvMSe88MCPIuXioLygbatMPoOr1OjeTPkH9nhIiCSPm7Bwd6enL9SGGWJvKPq-qcqTjz3i8), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESYwHrOzAVhfC6ZNe-INnpA_9MMTpC6WJ2r94aegqcrvtkbo7faAhJWULL8c3t1lRrwzR4iqMeMyrcjPH_CIk9Fv-ZLLYpX77E7oFQQOkocHFqU0iKpb6oZpqCBtRfdApaZrTOMw), [3](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESegHrOzAVyD1JtwByMcAWIBTF0ydgmaGQp-GyOSHURvg_A8MNR08ZTyaiv2euhFPTVMcC1NuvqSUqlsD2mF4eKawdDClK30odxUqv-Tx0e-Hw15gyF_34WiY6QIElr_6si0-jwPBFFyn4wF8tlkXlMcIcF5fE2pnETLPv), [4](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESTgHrOzAVj9mNQPCbUBgAALggxbMJHG7RlLystfXN-_YOqbNf6u7dGP-eQXgsFIKcOhXqv5is4Pg50HNu8GrepXHgjMZYbYHyaldT52wFhQ), [5](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESVQHrOzAViSAcpbzd8j0w9TyGXP26wLvk9SSkHa4AuPWS2SKK3y660rrt53Kc_fmIbizKgyN_q-LcL-ye4WAcsVDn3pTsqNraMFmdOQ9ut66_xC7Sbww)]

How It Works

* Evaluation Process: Applicants submit an expression of interest, sign legal agreements, provide technical evidence, and run self-test tools against program requirements. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESuwEB6zswFRai9sJAHdfacExt5I84WcuS66u2ZYT4emRG9th0KsvmyjdC4CbGmVoVPjQ7xDVCvDSu4vqnxoCgM3qDj23FkTydGzAJGZT6O6_fp5uAshWHgRJ9lNc3Un1OykhuH5lgP1y6iwbhDIvPSUQ1H9rU3pmUeBH2_vOYIiuGuYYbG0kifQ8YpFA0u2B6nk-DbnNtoDHEmFYvKscu6qUv0T4UvjdjpG-hvKzjOfvJobQGIgv8sECkmU81), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESdAHrOzAVcOIhTlkuurqIjQZbX7LZb7YpYwWhyUaH9_ztL_rnj7P4XHD5q3EidjPCgwxyY0WhOB25AY-w0NwTUWvMSe88MCPIuXioLygbatMPoOr1OjeTPkH9nhIiCSPm7Bwd6enL9SGGWJvKPq-qcqTjz3i8)]
* Trust & Security: Only conforming generator products can receive production claim-signing certificates from approved CAs, creating end-to-end tamper evidence for digital media. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESggEB6zswFWMxog3GTPYX2rNEPwb0zpqq_2-hRSCedQM2wbOyVZUDiswtZP-ZRN8QFSrDkmr9QVmyd3jnFy0iI4dSQQLmx3DsTxGAKV3jw_lLOc5uOJwKPbkTmg-WU14GzUaXfd41plx_WKgMzLvZ9G-gpm1I09NPYsFgqCTPGyJxP11H), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESegHrOzAVyD1JtwByMcAWIBTF0ydgmaGQp-GyOSHURvg_A8MNR08ZTyaiv2euhFPTVMcC1NuvqSUqlsD2mF4eKawdDClK30odxUqv-Tx0e-Hw15gyF_34WiY6QIElr_6si0-jwPBFFyn4wF8tlkXlMcIcF5fE2pnETLPv)]

If you want, I can help you:

* Look up specific vendors or products on the Conforming Products List
* Explain the difference between Level 1 and Level 2 assurance levels
* Detail how to submit a product for conformance testing
